answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, with transition mass attenuated at each step. A sybil cluster lacking many honest attestations creates a sparse external cut; its low conductance limits probability flow across the boundary. Min-cut transitivity therefore bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting weight by its cut capacity and imported trust, so names such as saffron, sparrow, or karst cannot amplify colluding identities.
